note: Shared fixture for the direction algorithm, run by BOTH implementations — the Swift one in this repo and the TypeScript port in packages/web. A case that passes in one and fails in the other is the entire reason this file exists. Adding a case here must make both suites exercise it with no edit to either. directionallyMarked does NOT strip first and is NOT idempotent — marking already-marked text doubles every mark. Callers must strip before marking; the Swift app does this in TextInserter. The round-trip invariant below is that pipeline, and both suites assert it for every case.
invariants: For every case: directionallyMarked(stripping(expected)) === expected. This is the real pipeline — strip, then mark — and it proves marks never accumulate across round trips. Both suites assert it for every case automatically.
directionallyMarked is not idempotent on its own. Marking text that already carries marks doubles them. Strip first, always.
Pure Persian with no Latin gets the RLM and the terminator only. Pure English gets nothing at all. No marks are added where they earn nothing.

cases.name: pure-persian-no-terminator
cases.why: RTL with no Latin earns the base-direction mark only. Nothing is isolated because there is nothing to isolate, and the last character is a letter, so no terminator is appended.

cases.name: pure-persian-full-stop
cases.why: A sentence-final full stop is a neutral character with no following strong neighbour, so it falls back to paragraph direction and renders at the wrong end. The trailing RLM gives it one.

cases.name: pure-persian-question-mark
cases.why: Same as the full stop, for the Persian question mark. A Persian reader sees a misplaced ؟ as the start of the line.

cases.name: pure-persian-guillemet
cases.why: » is in the terminator set. The guillemets themselves are neither RTL nor Latin, so no isolate is opened around them.

cases.name: pure-english-unchanged
cases.why: No RTL anywhere, so the whole function is a no-op. Pure English gets no marks at all.

cases.name: pure-english-no-punctuation-unchanged
cases.why: Same: no RTL, nothing to fix, nothing added.

cases.name: persian-with-one-latin-word
cases.input: می‌خواهم این PDF را باز کنم
cases.why: The canonical case. Without the isolate the bidi algorithm flings PDF to the visual start or end of the line, changing what the sentence appears to say.

cases.name: latin-multi-word-run-stays-one-unit
cases.input: من از Claude Code استفاده می‌کنم.
cases.why: The space between two Latin words is kept inside the run because a Latin character follows it, so a product name is isolated as one unit rather than two that can be reordered against each other.

cases.name: version-number
cases.why: Digits extend a run, and '.' is a connector kept because a digit follows it. 16.2 must not split into 16 and 2 with a neutral between them.

cases.name: latin-run-then-sentence-final-stop
cases.input: آن را باز کن با Preview.
cases.why: The decisive connector case. '.' is a connector, but nothing Latin follows it, so the run ends before it. Swallowing the full stop into the isolate would place it at the wrong end of the line.

cases.name: latin-run-at-start-of-persian-line
cases.why: Without the leading RLM a line that opens with a Latin word is resolved left-to-right in its entirety.

cases.name: accented-latin-and-dotted-name
cases.input: من از Node.js و café استفاده می‌کنم.
cases.why: é is inside the 0xC0–0x24F accented-Latin range, so it is a Latin letter here. Node.js keeps its dot because 'j' follows it. Two separate runs, each isolated.

cases.name: connector-not-followed-by-latin-ends-the-run
cases.why: Pins the connector rule exactly: ':' is a connector but '/' is neither a Latin letter nor a digit, so the run ends at 'https'. The '//' stays outside any isolate. Ugly but correct, and a port that 'improves' it has diverged.

cases.name: multi-line-marked-per-line
cases.why: The bidi algorithm resolves per paragraph, so one mark at the top would not govern the lines below it. Each line is marked independently. Line one ends in PDI, which is not a terminator, so it gets no trailing RLM.

cases.name: multi-line-latin-only-line-untouched
cases.why: A line with no RTL in it is returned as-is even when another line in the same block has RTL. Per-line, not per-string.

strippingCases.name: strips-all-three-marks
strippingCases.expected: من از Claude Code استفاده می‌کنم.
strippingCases.why: RLM, FSI and PDI all come out, leaving the logical text a terminal or code editor can show without literal escapes.

strippingCases.name: unmarked-text-unchanged
strippingCases.input: می‌خواهم این PDF را باز کنم
strippingCases.expected: می‌خواهم این PDF را باز کنم
strippingCases.why: Stripping is safe to call on anything.

strippingCases.name: strips-marks-across-lines
strippingCases.why: Stripping is a plain replacement over the whole string, lines included.

strippingCases.name: strips-doubled-marks
strippingCases.expected: من از Claude Code استفاده می‌کنم.
strippingCases.why: What text looks like when someone marked it twice without stripping. Stripping removes every occurrence, so the damage is recoverable — which is why the pipeline is strip-then-mark rather than a guard inside marking.
